# Project workflow

Read AGENTS.md for the project workflow and Beads skill.

○ trial-0o0 · Export protocol 1 accepted receipt details   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  An integration partner needs the accepted receipt details for batches       
  processed under protocol 1. Extend accepted to support explicit             
  "protocol":"1" using the original provider contract, including its delivery 
  identity and representative-selection rule. That contract shipped with the  
  initial account-count issue. Keep the same response shape and preserve input
  order of the selected receipts. Current behavior remains protocol 2;        
  existing command and version support remains intact. Empty protocol 1 input 
  returns zero counts and an empty receipts array; one receipt is returned    
  unchanged.

The provider permanently adopted protocol 2 and the integration owner approved it as current. An omitted "protocol" in a request selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL ("2"); an explicit supported version selects that version and stays supported after a newer current version is introduced ("1" remains supported). Commands count, summary, and accepted share analyze(q), which returns (protocol, receipts, accepted_list) and dispatches on version via accepted_receipts(protocol, receipts); accepted_list is None for an unsupported version, and every command then returns {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. count and summary share receipt_counts() and return exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count} reporting the protocol actually used. accepted (issue trial-zee) returns exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, receipts}: the counts equal summary for the same request, and receipts holds the accepted representatives selected under the chosen protocol, unchanged (fields, timestamp spelling, payload) and in original input order; empty input gives receipts [] and zero counts; a single receipt is returned unchanged. Per-version rules: protocol 1 = accepted_receipts_v1, contract in vendor/protocol-1.md: identity=(account_id, delivery_id), same delivery_id under different accounts is a separate delivery; accept EARLIEST occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point. Protocol 2 = accepted_receipts_v2, contract in vendor/protocol-2.md: identity=delivery_id alone across all accounts, same ID under another account is another receipt of the same delivery; accept LATEST occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point. Both keep accepted receipts unchanged in original input order; the rule applies to the whole supplied set regardless of receipt dates. Timestamps parsed via parse_instant() (RFC3339, Z or numeric offset, compared as UTC). When adding protocol N: add accepted_receipts_vN plus vendor/protocol-N.md, add its branch in accepted_receipts() so count, summary, and accepted all pick it up, add N to SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS, and change CURRENT_PROTOCOL only when N becomes current. Public suites name protocols explicitly; run python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/<file>.json (accepted_2.json, count_1.json, summary_1.json, summary_2.json); regression tests in tests/ (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests; test_accepted.py covers accepted). Earlier state preserved under key courier-relay/protocol-versioning-history-protocol-1-current. Source: issues trial-vbm, trial-dvi, trial-u7q, trial-zee; vendor/protocol-1.md, vendor/protocol-2.md.

HISTORICAL (superseded 2026-09-07 by issue trial-u7q, which made protocol 2 current; see courier-relay/protocol-versioning for the standing agreement). Courier Relay protocol versioning as of issues trial-vbm and trial-dvi (main.py): CURRENT_PROTOCOL="1" and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS=("1",). An omitted "protocol" in a request selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL; an explicit supported version selects that version and stays supported after a newer current version is introduced. Commands count (original single-account use) and summary (cross-account batch, issue trial-dvi) share one body, receipt_counts(), which returns exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count} and dispatches on version via accepted_receipts(protocol, receipts); unsupported versions return {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Protocol 1 is accepted_receipts_v1, contract in vendor/protocol-1.md: identity=(account_id, delivery_id) so the same delivery_id under different accounts is a separate delivery and a batch may mix any number of accounts; accept earliest occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point, accepted keep original fields/order. Timestamps parsed via parse_instant() (RFC3339, Z or numeric offset, compared as UTC). Public suites name protocols explicitly; run python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/<file>.json. Source: issues trial-vbm and trial-dvi, vendor/protocol-1.md.

  issues.

  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner  
  approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:    
                                                                              
  Protocol 2: delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the
  same ID under another account is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly  
  one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the  
  latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id.  
  All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt  
  retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present       
  accepted receipts in their original input order. This identity contract     
  comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account         
  attribution alone does not change that guarantee.                           
                                                                              
  Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit       
  "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the  
  original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol
  used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of    
  receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and
  zero duplicates.
